outlook.nextStep: Tonight's after-the-bell trio of Nvidia, CrowdStrike, and Salesforce earnings is the single biggest near-term catalyst, arriving right after a hotter-than-expected PCE inflation print revived Fed rate-hike chatter; Friday's Jackson Hole speech from Chair Warsh is the other event worth close attention for rates and macro. The Clarity Act's now-firm September 15 Senate vote and the memory-chip competitive dynamics with China are probably better treated as slower-moving stories to watch than as near-term events to react to.

signals.title: Nvidia, CrowdStrike, and Salesforce all report after tonight's close
signals.body: Three closely watched names report Q2 results after the bell today. Nvidia is expected to post $92-98B in revenue (roughly doubling year-over-year), with price targets clustering near $306; options markets are pricing a smaller-than-usual post-earnings move. CrowdStrike and Salesforce round out the trio, with prediction markets showing 90%+ odds all three beat estimates, though CrowdStrike's average one-day reaction to earnings has skewed slightly negative in recent quarters even on beats.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether tonight's results confirm continued AI-infrastructure demand or reignite the ROI-fear narrative from earlier this summer

signals.title: Hotter-than-expected PCE print revives Fed rate-hike chatter ahead of Jackson Hole
signals.body: This morning's PCE inflation report showed core prices up 3.3% year-over-year and headline PCE up 3.7%, both a touch stronger than economists expected. The data strengthens the case for a possible Fed rate hike rather than the rate cut some had been positioning for, just two days before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, where he's expected to stay characteristically light on forward guidance.
signals.focus: worth watching closely whether Friday's speech leans hawkish given today's inflation surprise, given how sensitive yields have been to Warsh's prior public comments

signals.title: Memory chips diverge from the broader semiconductor rally on China competition fears
signals.body: While most chip names rallied into Nvidia's report, Micron, SanDisk, and SK Hynix all slipped in premarket trading, weighed down by renewed concerns about Chinese memory maker YMTC and its upcoming IPO. Micron separately announced the promotion of two senior executives, including a new COO, as it looks to solidify its leadership team.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the China competitive threat is a near-term overhang or a longer structural risk to memory pricing power

signals.title: Bitcoin holds near $79,000 as Clarity Act disputes remain unresolved ahead of September 15 vote
signals.body: Bitcoin has cooled after briefly topping $81,000 earlier this week, the highest level in over three months. The Senate's cloture vote on the Clarity Act is now firmly scheduled for September 15, but negotiators still have unresolved disagreements over illicit-finance protections, stablecoin reward provisions, and government-ethics language that could affect the bill's final shape and its odds of clearing the 60-vote threshold.
signals.focus: worth watching whether the unresolved policy disputes cap further upside heading into the vote, versus treating the current level as a stable higher base

signals.title: Tesla, Uber, and Waymo win Nevada robotaxi approval as China's humanoid complex rallies
signals.body: The Nevada Transportation Authority approved permits for Tesla, Uber, and Waymo to operate commercial robotaxi services in the state, extending the autonomous-vehicle buildout to another market. Separately, UBTECH and the broader China humanoid-robotics complex bounced back today after recent weakness, part of a sector-wide recovery.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual robotics names as noise relative to the multi-year capital-flow trend into the space

signals.title: Oracle gets an upside catalyst call from Citi after its steep selloff
signals.body: Citi opened an 'upside 90-day catalyst watch' on Oracle while maintaining its Buy rating and $330 price target, following a selloff that has taken the stock down roughly 55% from its all-time high last October. Separately, Microsoft deepened its AI partnerships this week with a long-term collaboration with Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN, while reports surfaced that China's Moonshot AI is in talks with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google to host its Kimi K3 model.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether Citi's call marks a genuine inflection for Oracle or is early relative to the stock's ongoing capex and free-cash-flow concerns
